clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Sabrina presented with a cheerful and cooperative affect; however, her attention span was notably limited, with frequent distractibility requiring consistent redirection. Her muscle tone was assessed to be within normal limits, and she demonstrated a full range of motion across major joints. Despite this, engagement patterns varied, with Sabrina showing more responsiveness during structured activities compared to self-directed ones where she sought intermittent guidance. She exhibited fine motor coordination challenges, evidenced by her need for hand-over-hand assistance during tasks involving visual-motor integration. Sabrina needed maximal verbal and visual cues to sustain attention on complex tasks. These behavioral observations necessitated modifications to the testing environment, which were essential for achieving a valid assessment of her abilities.
